hero.headline: "Everyone normal has already done it!" — and your child is already going along with it?
hero.subheadline: "Everyone" isn't a fact. It's an illusion of a norm designed to make you follow rather than think. It's not an argument — it's pressure.

media.alt: A child trying to conform to an illusory group norm

pain.title: "Everyone" is a pressure word, not reality
pain.body:
"Everyone already handed it in", "everyone's already gone", "everyone normal has done it". In class, in the chat, among friends. The child might have doubts — but thinks: if everyone's doing it, I should too. The fear of being "different" turns out stronger than their own opinion.

This isn't a fact — it's a manufactured illusion of the norm. The word "everyone" is used as pressure, even though nobody checked. The child isn't shown reality — they're given the feeling that they're the only one who's "not like the others". Without the skill to notice this, they automatically conform.

The result — decisions are made not independently, but out of fear of standing out. The child doesn't even ask "who exactly is everyone?" — they just go along so as not to fall behind.
